prompt: hpx::future destructor blocking behavior vs std::future
answer:
- **`hpx::future`**: Its destructor does **not block**, even if the asynchronous operation is unfinished and `.get()`/`.wait()` was not called. HPX deliberately diverges from the standard here so that futures have uniform semantics regardless of how they were created.  
  Sources: [HPX proposal](https://open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2017/p0701r1.html), [HPX discussion](https://github.com/STEllAR-GROUP/hpx/pull/3205)

- **`std::future`**: The destructor generally does not block, **except** for a future returned by `std::async` when it holds the last reference to an unfinished shared state. In that case, destruction blocks until the task completes. Futures from `std::promise` and `std::packaged_task` do not have this blocking-destructor behavior.  
  Source: [Microsoft Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/standard-library/future?view=msvc-170)

Thus, unlike `std::future`, an `hpx::future` destructor is intended not to wait for unfinished work.
